title: Split the exponential
text: $$e^{y-x}=e^y e^{\left(-x\right)}$$, so the equation is $$\frac{dy}{dx}=e^y e^{\left(-x\right)}$$. Separate to get $$e^{\left(-y\right)} dy=e^{\left(-x\right)} dx$$.

title: Integrate and solve
text: Integrating gives $$-e^{\left(-y\right)}=-e^{\left(-x\right)}+C$$. At $$x=0$$, $$y=0$$ this is $$-1=-1+C$$, so $$C=0$$. Then $$e^{\left(-y\right)}=e^{\left(-x\right)}$$, so $$y=x$$.
